To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a fast solver for the L21-regularized bio magnetic inverse problems, and we propose new estimators for multitasking regression in the presence non white heteroscedastic Gaussian noise.

(1) we propose speed improvements of L21 penalized sparse regression algorithms, and we connect them to the asymptotic behavior of proximal algorithms on manifolds (2) we design a multitask regression estimator, jointly estimating the solution and the noise, which we analyze and connect to Schatten norms smoothing

1) we propose speed improvements for iterative solvers used in sparse high dimensional regression; 2) we propose a new concomitant estimator for multitask regression, which is able to model non white Gaussian noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new statistical and numerical tools to solve the bio magnetic inverse problem and to improve its interpretation.
the statistical and computational aspects of sparse high dimensional regression, with applications in M/EEG inverse problems and source imaging.
the development of statistical and numerical tools to improve the reconstruction of neural activity from M/EEG measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this thesis is a major contribution to the field of M/EEGs source imaging, and that the proposed improvements and novel methods are a major contribution to this field.
the proposed methods and analysis are of great interest for the community working on the bio magnetic inverse problem and the related sparse high dimensional statistical inference.
the proposed improvements allow to process M/EEG data in real time, and to estimate the noise covariance matrices in a more statistically efficient way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is a new approach for a new application of machine learning.
we have proposed a new framework for the analysis of M/EEGs data.
we provide a set of tools to solve sparse multitask problems in a faster and more accurate way, and apply these tools to a neuroimaging problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L21 regularizer is not a mere mathematical tool, but a powerful and efficient tool to solve the bio magnetic inverse problem in the presence of non white noise.
the L21 regularization, although popular, is not the only way to impose a sparse solution in the bio magnetic inverse problem: other approaches are available.
the combination of a careful design of the optimization algorithms, with a better statistical modeling of the data can lead to more efficient and accurate source localization methods.
